headline: Open Access Coastal Heritage and Wildlife Viewing
reservation: The Bonavista Peninsula generally does not require a peninsula-wide entry permit, but individual historic sites like the Ryan Premises may require admission. High-demand accommodations in Trinity or Bonavista often book out months in advance for the summer season. Always check with the Newfoundland and Labrador provincial tourism office for site-specific seasonal closures.

days.title: Trinity Bight and Historic Architecture

stops.name: Skerwink Trail
stops.detail: Walk the rugged coastal loop near Port Rexton for views of sea stacks and potential whale sightings in the bay.

stops.name: Trinity National Historic Site
stops.detail: Explore the well-preserved 18th and 19th-century architecture of this coastal merchant town, including the historic parish church.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for local coastal roads; conditions vary.
days.note: The Skerwink Trail features steep cliff edges; maintain a safe distance from the rim.

days.title: Coastal Cliffs and Puffin Colonies

stops.name: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit this iconic 19th-century provincial landmark where John Cabot is said to have first sighted land.

stops.name: Elliston Puffin Site
stops.detail: Observe one of North America's most accessible Atlantic Puffin colonies from the rocky outcrops near the shoreline.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the loop between Bonavista and Elliston; conditions vary.
days.note: Puffin sightings are highly seasonal, typically peaking between late June and early August.

days.title: Marine History and Geological Marvels

stops.name: Ryan Premises National Historic Site
stops.detail: Learn about the international cod fishery history within these restored 19th-century merchant buildings.

stops.name: Dungeon Provincial Park
stops.detail: View the massive collapsed sea cave and natural twin arches carved by the Atlantic surf into the coastal cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for town-adjacent travel; conditions vary.
days.note: Coastal wind speeds can be high; dress in layers even during mid-summer months.

intel.title: Seasonal Site Availability
intel.text: Many provincial historic sites and local museums operate strictly from mid-May to early October. Verify individual opening dates for the Cape Bonavista Lighthouse and Ryan Premises.

intel.title: Bonavista and Clarenville Hubs
intel.text: Fuel is readily available in Clarenville and the town of Bonavista, but stations are sparse along the Discovery Trail (Route 230). Ensure a full tank before exploring the secondary coastal loops.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacities
intel.text: Parking at the Skerwink Trailhead in Port Rexton is limited and can fill during peak morning hours in July. Alternative parking may be found in the village, following local signage.

intel.title: Variable Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is strong in Trinity and Bonavista but often drops to zero in low-lying coves or along the rugged northern tip. Download maps for offline use before leaving Clarenville.

intel.title: Iceberg and Whale Season
intel.text: Iceberg viewing typically peaks in late May to June, while whale watching is best in July. Timing varies significantly each year based on sea ice and water temperature.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Gander (YQX), drive east to Clarenville for supplies, then proceed to your base in Trinity or Bonavista.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are suitable for main paved routes, though some coastal viewpoints involve gravel roads; check rental agreements for unpaved road coverage.
plan.goldenHour: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse cliffs during the summer sunset.
